lines: {parent} still checks in on me when the village gets loud. They have a way of making feel at home anywhere.
{parent} knows when the village gets too loud for me. That kind of care makes me feel good.
When there's trouble, <aqua>{parent}</aqua> is who I usually trust.
I keep an eye on <aqua>{child}</aqua>. Around here, every child learns quickly which footsteps mean help.
{child} is one reason I watch the paths more closely than I used to.
Children learn the village by watching us. I try to give <aqua>{child}</aqua> something good to copy.
<aqua>{sibling}</aqua> and I do not always agree, but I would still stand between them and trouble.
<aqua>{sibling}</aqua> can test my patience and still have my loyalty.
I know every way <aqua>{sibling}</aqua> can annoy me, and every reason I would defend them.
<aqua>{grandparent}</aqua> taught the family which paths are safe after dark. Some advice survives longer than the person who first said it.
<aqua>{grandparent}</aqua> remembers roads I only know as stories. I listen when they warn me.
<aqua>{grandparent_possessive} old advice still keeps my feet out of trouble. <aqua>{grandparent}</aqua>
When I think about <aqua>{descendant}</aqua>, I try to leave the village a little kinder than I found it.
<aqua>{descendant}</aqua> makes the future feel like a real place, not just a word.
I want <aqua>{descendant}</aqua> to inherit more than locked doors and nervous bells.
<aqua>{extended_relative}</aqua> is not in my house every night, but family branches still share the same weather.
<aqua>{extended_relative}</aqua> may live under another roof, but kinship still knocks when trouble comes.
Family stretches farther than a doorstep. <aqua>{extended_relative}</aqua> proves that often enough.
We still say <aqua>{deceased_family_possessive}</aqua> name when the village gathers. Remembering is a kind of shelter.
<aqua>{deceased_family_possessive}</aqua> memory still has a chair in this village.
We speak of <aqua>{deceased_family}</aqua> carefully. Grief is still part of the household. <aqua>{deceased_family_possessive}</aqua>
<aqua>{relative}</aqua> is family. That is enough to make me careful about who asks.
Ask about <aqua>{relative}</aqua> with respect, and maybe I will answer.
Family names are not loose coins. <aqua>{relative}</aqua> matters to me.
<aqua>{partner}</aqua> makes the village feel less like a place I survive and more like a place I choose.
With <aqua>{partner}</aqua>, even a hard day has somewhere softer to end.
<aqua>{partner}</aqua> makes the village feel less like walls and more like home.
I keep finding reasons to pass near <aqua>{crush}</aqua>. Maybe it is foolish. Maybe foolish things keep people kind.
I notice when <aqua>{crush}</aqua> crosses the square. I pretend not to, badly.
<aqua>{crush}</aqua> makes ordinary errands feel suspiciously important.
<aqua>{dating_partner}</aqua> and I are seeing where the road goes. Slowly is fine when the road matters.
<aqua>{dating_partner}</aqua> and I are taking it carefully. Careful things can still be brave.
I like walking beside <aqua>{dating_partner}</aqua>. The road feels less noisy that way.
<aqua>{fiance}</aqua> and I are trying to plan a future sturdy enough to survive this place.
<aqua>{fiance}</aqua> and I are planning more than a ceremony. We are planning a life that holds.
When I say <aqua>{fiance_possessive}</aqua> name, the future feels less theoretical. <aqua>{fiance}</aqua>
<aqua>{romantic_spouse}</aqua> knows which silences mean I am tired and which mean I need help. That is a rare comfort.
<aqua>{romantic_spouse}</aqua> knows my storms and still keeps a light on.
Home sounds different when <aqua>{romantic_spouse}</aqua> is there.
<aqua>{ex_partner}</aqua> and I had our season. Some roads part before they turn cruel, and that can be mercy.
<aqua>{ex_partner}</aqua> and I learned what we could, then stopped before kindness ran out.
Some endings with <aqua>{ex_partner}</aqua> still deserve gentleness.
<aqua>{late_partner}</aqua> is gone, but some mornings I still make room for them in my thoughts.
<aqua>{late_partner}</aqua> is gone, but love leaves habits behind.
I still carry <aqua>{late_partner_possessive}</aqua> name carefully. <aqua>{late_partner}</aqua>
<aqua>{partner}</aqua> is not a market rumor. Ask gently, or do not ask.
Do not turn <aqua>{partner}</aqua> into gossip. Some things deserve a closed door.
If you ask about <aqua>{partner}</aqua>, ask like the answer belongs to a person.
<aqua>{parent}</aqua> says I should stay where the bell can hear me.
<aqua>{parent}</aqua> says the safest place is where someone can see me.
<aqua>{parent}</aqua> can find me even when I am pretending very hard to hide.
<aqua>{sibling}</aqua> thinks they are faster than me. They are not always right.
<aqua>{sibling}</aqua> says I am little. I say I am compact.
<aqua>{sibling}</aqua> runs fast, but I know better shortcuts.
<aqua>{grandparent}</aqua> knows stories that start before my bed was even made.
<aqua>{grandparent}</aqua> tells stories with extra corners in them.
<aqua>{grandparent}</aqua> remembers when everything was somehow uphill.
<aqua>{cousin}</aqua> says we are related enough to share chores. I think that sounds suspicious.
<aqua>{cousin}</aqua> says chores are easier with two people. I think they mean me.
<aqua>{cousin}</aqua> knows games that suspiciously look like work.
